policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 3:4 renders the relative clause as 'the things which we command', with no dative object; the ASV supplies 'you' where it is read (3:6 'we command you'), so the absence here answers the shorter lemma without + ὑμῖν.

ASV 3:6 reads 'in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ'; the possessive 'our' renders ἡμῶν, which the omitting reading lacks. The verse's note ('read ye') bears on the verb of receiving, not on this pronoun.

ASV text reads 'the tradition which they received of us' — third person plural, which excludes παρελάβετε (r01); the mapped note 'Some ancient authorities read ye' records that second-person reading as the alternative, confirming it is not the text rendered. Between παρελάβοσαν and παρέλαβον the English is identical, both being 'they received', so the choice is not distinguished.
Genitive νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας and accusative νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν both render as ASV 'night and day'; English has no way to mark the case distinction and no note is mapped here.

ASV 3:12 reads 'we command and exhort in the Lord Jesus Christ' — 'in' for ἐν with no possessive; the alternative διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν would give 'by our Lord', and the ASV shows neither 'by' nor 'our'.
ἐγκακήσητε and ἐκκακήσητε are orthographic forms of the same verb with the same sense; ASV 'be not weary in well-doing' renders either identically.

ASV 3:14 continues 'note that man, that ye have no company with him' — a subordinate clause with no coordinating 'and'. The καὶ μὴ reading goes with the imperative construction ('and have no company'), which the ASV's subordination does not render.

ASV 3:14 renders 'that ye have no company with him', a subordinate infinitive clause dependent on 'note that man'; the imperative συναναμίγνυσθε would give an independent command, which the ASV does not have.
ASV 3:18 ends 'be with you all.' with no closing 'Amen'; the ASV prints Amen where it is read, so its absence answers the lemma without + Ἀμήν.
